items.title: Human-Centered AI Education for Viksit Bharat @2047: Reimagining Teachers, Learners and Future-Ready Schools
items.abstract: Abstract: Artificial Intelligence is reshaping how societies function, communicate, learn and innovate, and India stands at a particularly consequential point in this shift. The arrival of generative AI, adaptive learning platforms and intelligent digital tools presents the country with both a rare opportunity and a demanding policy challenge on its path toward Viksit Bharat @2047. Education sits at the heart of this challenge, because the citizens, workers and innovators who will carry that vision forward are being shaped right now, inside today's classrooms. This conceptual paper asks how Artificial Intelligence can genuinely strengthen India's education system without eroding the human qualities that make learning meaningful: agency, creativity, ethics and social responsibility. Drawing on an integrative reading of policy documents and international literature - UNESCO's AI competency frameworks, OECD perspectives on AI literacy, India's National Education Policy 2020, the IndiaAI Mission, the World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025, ILO research on generative AI and employment, and the author's own practitioner book AI and Us - the paper argues that the real question is not whether AI will replace teachers, but whether schools can build a working partnership between teachers, learners and AI. The paper introduces a Human-Centered AI Education Framework built around six interlocking dimensions: AI Literacy, AI-Augmented Pedagogy, Human Skills, Ethical and Responsible Use, Inclusive Digital Infrastructure, and Continuous Professional Learning. It also sketches a Teacher-AI-Student ecosystem in which AI takes on assistive and analytical work while teachers hold on to pedagogical, relational and ethical authority. Viksit Bharat @2047, the paper contends, does not just need citizens who are skilled at using AI - it needs citizens who are AI-literate, critical, creative, ethical and socially engaged. The paper closes with policy recommendations aimed at schools, teacher-education institutions, government bodies and educational technology developers.

items.title: Human-Centred AI for Sustainable Digital Governance in India: A Review of Digital Public Services.
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to improve public service delivery through automation, data analysis, decision support and digital interaction. In India, Digital India, Digital Public Infrastructure and national AI initiatives have created opportunities to make government services more efficient, accessible and responsive. At the same time, AI-enabled public services raise concerns related to privacy, transparency, bias, accessibility, accountability and citizen trust. This paper examines how a Human-Centred AI (HCAI) approach can support sustainable digital governance in India through a structured review of secondary literature. Recent peer-reviewed studies, government reports and institutional publications are examined using thematic analysis. The review focuses on citizen-centric service delivery, accessibility and inclusion, transparency and explainability, privacy and security, fairness, citizen trust, and human oversight. The findings indicate that AI can support intelligent service discovery, conversational assistance, multilingual interaction, personalisation and routine administrative processing. However, technological capability alone does not guarantee better public services. AI must be designed around citizen needs and supported by appropriate governance safeguards. Based on the synthesis, the paper proposes a conceptual Human-Centred AI Framework with five interconnected dimensions: human needs, inclusive digital experience, responsible AI, accountable governance and sustainable public value. The paper concludes that India's AI-enabled digital governance should balance technological innovation with accessibility, privacy, fairness, transparency, human oversight and public trust.

items.title: Human-inspired Route Selection for Efficient Social Robot Navigation in Narrow Spaces
items.abstract: Narrow human environments are challenging for social robot navigation, where distance-optimal shortcut routes to destination are frequently blocked by people in the aisles. People in these situations select the appropriate route between detour and shortcut in an efficient and socially-aware way, by balancing their extra effort (if choosing detour) and the required effort from the person on the way to make space to pass. Similar balance strategy is utilized when people decide the politeness of the request utterance to compensate for the way yielding effort from others. Inspired by this human balance strategy, we developed a decision-making methodological framework for socially-aware high-level path planning and interaction utterance when the robot navigates in narrow shared spaces and implemented it onto a humanoid mobile robot. In order to demonstrate the transparency and utility of this framework, we present a specific instantiation by conducting a set of human-robot experiments in a real store. Data from 30 people were collected via two field experiments to identify socially-acceptable parameters. Results of a within-participants study with 28 human customers interestingly demonstrated that the proposed socially-aware method was more time-efficient compared to the detour-only and shortcut-only strategies.

items.title: Human-Routed Handoffs in ChatGPT: A Possibly More Token-Efficient Procedure for Cross-Surface Work
items.abstract: This paper proposes a human-routed procedure for maintaining continuity across ChatGPT conversations and work surfaces.Derived from developing papers and a screenplay, it separates two objects: a Dump preserves relevant discussion; a Handoff directs the next operation. Verbatim and Summary Dumps offer different levels of fidelity and compression.Two controls govern the procedure: Authority Space bounds jurisdiction; Goodwill bounds optimization after sufficiency. Handoffs must remain checkable, with review proportionate to consequences and the object’s validity conditions.The procedure may reduce reconstruction and token use while preserving human judgment and responsibility. These benefits are practical observations rather than quantified or universal claims. The proposal is offered for adaptation, testing, correction, or rejection.

items.title: Hybrid feature selection with SHAP-based explainable AI for interpretable phishing website detection
items.abstract: Phishing websites remain a significant cybersecurity threat, exploiting users through deceptive web interfaces and continuously evolving attack strategies. Despite the effectiveness of machine learning approaches, many existing solutions suffer from limited interpretability, redundant feature representations, and evaluation practices that may lead to overly optimistic performance estimates. This study proposes a phishing website detection framework that integrates hybrid feature selection with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). The proposed approach combines Mutual Information, Χ², and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based feature importance to identify the most informative and discriminative features from complementary statistical, information-theoretic, and model-driven perspectives. The framework was evaluated using the PhiUSIIL dataset and further validated on an external URL-only dataset to assess generalization capability. To ensure reliable performance estimation and prevent information leakage, feature selection was performed independently within each fold of a 10-fold stratified cross-validation procedure. Five machine learning classifiers, namely Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, were evaluated using classifier-specific feature subsets generated independently within the cross-validation procedure. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid feature selection framework substantially reduces the feature space while maintaining predictive performance comparable to that achieved using all available features. Across the evaluated classifiers, XGBoost provided the most balanced overall performance. Additional analyses showed that the near-perfect performance observed on the PhiUSIIL dataset was dataset-dependent, with lower performance obtained on the external dataset and under an oracle-informed worst-case feature perturbation scenario, highlighting the sensitivity of the framework under more demanding evaluation conditions. SHAP further improves model interpretability by providing both global and local explanations of feature contributions while supporting the feature selection process. Overall, the findings demonstrate that integrating statistical, information-theoretic, and explainability-driven feature selection can substantially reduce feature dimensionality while preserving predictive performance and improving model interpretability. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and computationally efficient basis for phishing website detection, while its practical deployment remains dependent on feature-extraction costs and validation under heterogeneous operational conditions.

items.title: Hyper-Personalization vs. Privacy Paradox: Balancing AI-Driven Customer Insights with Consumer Data Ethics and Trust
items.abstract: Abstract: The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence and machine learning has enabled organizations to achieve unprecedented levels of hyper-personalization, transforming how brands interact with consumers. However, this capability intensifies the privacy paradox, a phenomenon where consumers express profound concern for data privacy while simultaneously trading personal information for tailored experiences and immediate utility. This paper examines the complex equilibrium required to harness AI-driven customer insights without eroding consumer data ethics and organizational trust. Traditional data collection frameworks are increasingly inadequate in managing the granular, predictive datasets utilized by modern personalization algorithms. As predictive analytics decipher behavioral patterns, purchasing intent, and real-time location data, the ethical threshold for consent, transparency, and data minimization rises significantly. Organizations frequently struggle to balance the commercial imperatives of hyper-targeted engagement with regulatory compliance, such as the General Data Protection Regulation and evolving global privacy standards. This research investigates how opaque data practices and aggressive profiling lead to algorithmic fatigue, consumer alienation, and catastrophic trust erosion. The study analyzes the mechanics of transparent data stewardship, exploring how organizations can implement ethical AI frameworks that prioritize consumer agency, explicit consent architecture, and explainable algorithmic models. By adopting privacy-by-design principles and federated learning techniques, businesses can derive deep consumer insights without compromising individual anonymity or data security. Furthermore, the paper highlights the strategic advantage of ethical positioning, demonstrating that transparent data practices transform compliance from a legal burden into a distinct market differentiator. Methodologically, this study combines a comprehensive review of contemporary digital ethics literature with empirical case analyses of firms navigating data breaches versus those successfully cultivating trust-based personalization ecosystems. The findings reveal that sustainable customer lifetime value is directly correlated with perceived data fairness and control. Ultimately, the paper provides a strategic roadmap for leaders to align AI-driven marketing capabilities with robust ethical safeguards, ensuring that hyper-personalization fosters long-term brand loyalty rather than opportunistic exploitation.

items.title: IMoKGNN: Dual-Stream Fusion of Generic and Task-Specific Language Model Features for Graph Neural Networks
items.abstract: Text-Attributed Graphs (TAGs) are prevalent in various real-world scenarios, where each node is associated with a text attribute. Representation learning on TAGs relies on a comprehensive understanding of both the textual attributes and the topological connections. Recent works have enhanced graph neural networks (GNNs) with pre-trained language models (PLMs) for textual attribute modeling, achieving promising results compared with shallow text representations such as BoW. With the advent of more powerful LLMs, how to effectively and efficiently inject the generic knowledge in LLMs into representation learning on TAGs still calls for systematic investigation. To this end, we first examine whether mainstream generative LLMs can provide high-quality generic text embeddings that can be directly used by downstream GNNs, and further explore their complementarity with the task-specific knowledge from a tuned PLM (TLM). Based on these observations, we propose a dual-channel knowledge fusion framework, named MoKGNN, to simultaneously leverage the generic semantic knowledge from LLMs and the task adaptation capability of TLM. Specifically, we design a dual-channel feature extraction module to learn generic and task-specific text representations separately. Next, we introduce a Knowledge Alignment Network to align the LLM embeddings with the TLM representations. Finally, MoKGNN adopts a global mixing weight to fuse the two channels, obtaining a unified node embedding for downstream GNN training. Moreover, we further analyze a key limitation of such early feature fusion under message passing: once heterogeneous text features are merged before neighborhood aggregation, source-specific noise and non-aligned semantics may be diffused together and become harder to disentangle and correct. Motivated by this observation, we propose IMoKGNN, a decoupled dual-stream framework that propagates LLM and TLM features in parallel with a shared GNN backbone and performs late fusion in logit space. Extensive experiments on five TAG datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approaches for both node classification and link prediction, and show that IMoKGNN yields more reliable improvements than MoKGNN.

items.title: Impact of AI-Enabled Features in Faculty Teaching Effectiveness in Google Classroom
items.abstract: Abstract The Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration into education is transforming traditional teaching and learning practices. Google Classroom, currently with AI-enabled features such as lesson-plan generation, quiz creation, rubric development, differentiated learning resources, and suggested feedback, provides faculty with special power to improve teaching efficiency and classroom management. This study examines the impact of AI-enabled features on faculty teaching effectiveness in Google Classroom. The study mainly focuses on how AI influences lesson planning, preparation time, assessment, feedback, personalization of learning, student engagement, and overall teaching effectiveness. The study can be conducted using a structured questionnaire among faculty members who use Google Classroom. The findings are expected to show that AI can reduce routine workload and support more efficient and personalized teaching. However, factors such as AI literacy, training, accuracy of AI-generated content, privacy concerns, and the need for human supervision may influence its effectiveness. Research on AI in education also emphasizes the importance of teacher professional development and responsible implementation.

items.title: Impact of AI-Enabled Features in Faculty Teaching Effectiveness in Google Classroom
items.abstract: Abstract The Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration into education is transforming traditional teaching and learning practices. Google Classroom, currently with AI-enabled features such as lesson-plan generation, quiz creation, rubric development, differentiated learning resources, and suggested feedback, provides faculty with special power to improve teaching efficiency and classroom management. This study examines the impact of AI-enabled features on faculty teaching effectiveness in Google Classroom. The study mainly focuses on how AI influences lesson planning, preparation time, assessment, feedback, personalization of learning, student engagement, and overall teaching effectiveness. The study can be conducted using a structured questionnaire among faculty members who use Google Classroom. The findings are expected to show that AI can reduce routine workload and support more efficient and personalized teaching. However, factors such as AI literacy, training, accuracy of AI-generated content, privacy concerns, and the need for human supervision may influence its effectiveness. Research on AI in education also emphasizes the importance of teacher professional development and responsible implementation.

items.title: Impact Of Artificial Intelligence-Based Fitness Applications On Physical Activity Participation And Health Behaviour Among Undergraduate Students In Federal Universities In North-West Nigeria
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI) based fitness applications on physical activity participation and health behaviour among the undergraduates of Federal Universities, North-West Nigeria. The four objectives, four research questions, and four null hypotheses were the compass of this study. For the study, a descriptive correlational survey research design was used. The population consisted of undergraduate students of a few Federal Universities in the Northwest Nigeria. 384 undergraduate students were chosen as respondents using a multistage sampling technique. The Artificial Intelligence Fitness Applications, Physical Activity and Health Behaviour Questionnaire (AIFAPHBQ) was used to gather data. The internal consistency of the instrument was evaluated by Cronbach's Alpha reliability technique and the overall reliability coefficient obtained was 0.84. It was endorsed by experts in the field of Physical and Health Education, Educational Technology, and Measurement and Evaluation. The mean and the standard deviation were used to solve the problems in the study, while the independent-samples t-test and Pearson Product Moment Correlation were applied to test the null hypotheses at 0.05 level of significance. Based on the results, the use of AI-based fitness apps among undergraduate students was at moderate level (Grand Mean = 2.84, SD = 0.76). Use of the AI fitness app was positively associated with physical activity participation (r = .61, p < .001) and health behaviour (r = .58, p < .001). The results also revealed that male students felt they were using AI based fitness apps slightly more than female students, but this was not statistically significant (t = 1.63, p = .104). The researchers found that there is significant potential for the use of AI fitness apps to boost physical activity participation and promote positive health behaviours among undergraduate students. It suggests that digital health education, implementing institutional wellness programmes, and enhancing access to relevant digital infrastructure should be encouraged to promote responsible and health-oriented use of AI-based fitness technologies at universities.

Systems like Unified Payments Interface and digital bank accounts connect millions of unbanked citizens to the formal financial network. Online portals make government paperwork fast, transparent, and paperless through platforms like Digital India and Digi Locker. Direct Benefit Transfers send subsidies straight to bank accounts, cutting out middlemen and stopping leaks. Digitalization is one of the most powerful development opportunities of our time. items.title: Impact of Generative AI on Formal Writing Skills of Undergraduate students
items.abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has significantly influenced students' approach to formal writing. The present research, titled “Impact of Generative AI on the Formal Writing Practices of Undergraduate Students,” tries to examine the extent, frequency, purposes, and perceived effects of Generative AI used by undergraduate students in formal writing. A descriptive survey research design along with a quantitative approach was applied. A structured online questionnaire was prepared using Google Forms to collect primary data from undergraduate students representing programmes such as B.A., BMS, BAF, B.Com., B.Sc. Computer Science, B.Sc. IT, Psychology, History, and B.A.M.M.C. A total of 108 responses were obtained. Non-probability convenience sampling was used, and responses were analysed on the basis of frequency and percentage analysis, along with interpretation of Likert-scale responses. The findings show that a considerable number of undergraduate students use Generative AI in formal writing practices, which is clear as 94 out of 108 respondents (86.9%) selecting previous use of Generative AI for formal writing. ChatGPT proved to be the most popular Generative AI tool used by the students, followed by Google Gemini and Claude. The study reveals students’ use of AI for generating ideas, drafting content, improving grammar and language, summarising information, and editing written work. This study is aimed at finding out the degree of AI help in formal writing, the level of students' improvement in their writing skills, confidence in writing without AI help, acceptance of AI-written content without major editing, and their readiness to keep using the tools. This study reveals the significance of Generative AI in the field of formal writing of undergraduates and the advantages, as well as possible drawbacks, connected to their dependence on the technology. These results can be helpful in studying the influence of Generative AI on the writing process of students and will help the educational institutions and teachers to encourage proper and ethical use of Generative AI by students.

items.title: Importance Of Science In National Development: Building The Foundation Of Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract: Science has emerged as one of the most influential forces shaping economic growth, social transformation and national progress in the twenty-first century. The development of modern societies is increasingly dependent on the ability to create scientific knowledge, translate that knowledge into technological innovations and ensure that these innovations reach different sections of society. For a country such as India, which is simultaneously addressing issues of economic development, population growth, employment, education, healthcare, agriculture, energy security and environmental sustainability, science has a particularly important role to play. Scientific advancement can provide evidence-based and innovative solutions to complex national challenges while also strengthening India's competitiveness in the global knowledge economy. The vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 represents India's aspiration to become a developed nation by the centenary of independence. This vision encompasses not merely higher economic growth but also improvements in human development, education, healthcare, infrastructure, employment, social equity, technological capability, environmental sustainability and quality of life. Science and technology can serve as connecting forces among these different dimensions of development. Advances in agricultural science can improve productivity and climate resilience; medical science can support affordable healthcare; digital technologies can improve access to public services and education; space science can support communication, navigation and disaster management; renewable-energy research can strengthen energy security; and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, robotics and quantum technologies can create new opportunities for innovation and economic growth. The present paper examines the multidimensional importance of science in India's development with particular reference to Viksit Bharat @2047. It adopts a descriptive and analytical approach based on secondary information obtained from policy documents, government reports, scientific institutions, educational literature and international development reports. The paper discusses the contribution of science to economic development, agriculture, healthcare, education, industry, digital transformation, space technology, renewable energy and environmental sustainability. It further explores the role of scientific education in developing curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving ability and innovation among young people. The paper also identifies significant challenges, including unequal access to scientific resources, the digital divide, inadequate research infrastructure in some areas, limited industry-academia collaboration, shortage of specialised human resources, brain drain and the gap between scientific research and its practical application. The paper argues that the achievement of Viksit Bharat @2047 requires a transition from a technology-consuming society to a knowledge-generating and innovation-driven society. items.title: IMPROVING THE METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK FOR FUNCTIONAL ASSESSMENT OF HUMANITARIAN DEMINING SPECIALIST PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT KITS
items.abstract: The article presents an improved methodological framework for the functional assessment of personal protective equipment (PPE) intended for humanitarian demining specialists. The relevance of the study is determined by the growing need for standardized and reproducible procedures for evaluating the ergonomic suitability, operational effectiveness, and functional compatibility of protective equipment used during mine action operations. Humanitarian demining activities are associated with increased physical, limited visibility, restricted mobility, and high operational risks; therefore, PPE must provide not only ballistic and fragmentation protection but also sufficient functionality for safe execution of demining tasks. The study analyzes the current Ukrainian regulatory and legal framework governing mine action activities and compares it with relevant international standards and technical recommendations. The conducted analysis demonstrates that existing Ukrainian legislation regulates organizational, managerial, and certification aspects of mine action but does not establish a dedicated methodology for evaluating the ergonomic and functional suitability of deminer PPE. This creates significant difficulties in conducting objective comparative testing and in making evidence-based decisions regarding operational applicability of protective equipment. The purpose of the research is to improve the methodological apparatus for functional evaluation of humanitarian demining PPE considering the requirements of Ukrainian legislation and international standards. The research methodology includes comparative regulatory analysis, classification of PPE systems, development of functional assessment procedures, and formalization of result interpretation algorithms. The proposed framework is based on the principles of functional representativeness, repeatability, traceability, and practical applicability of testing results. PPE systems are classified into light and heavy categories depending on their protective structure, mobility restrictions, and operational characteristics. The methodology introduces a structured matrix of functional tests, including emergency quick-release assessment, visor visibility evaluation, finger dexterity testing, manipulation with probing tools, mobility assessment, posture transition evaluation, and control of dangerous gaps between protective elements during movement. Particular attention is devoted to defining scoring criteria, minimum admissible thresholds, participant selection requirements, and averaging algorithms for individual and group assessment results. Mandatory and additional tests are differentiated according to PPE category and operational conditions. The methodology also establishes formalized rules for determining whether a PPE configuration satisfies functional suitability requirements. The practical applicability of the proposed approach is demonstrated through comparative assessment of two PPE configurations differing in torso protection design. items.title: Indirect associations involving four work-motivation dimensions between perceived organizational climate and work engagement among geriatric nursing assistants in China: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Population ageing has increased demand for long-term care, yet evidence on organizational and motivational correlates of work engagement among geriatric nursing assistants in China remains limited. Using convenience sampling, this cross-sectional survey recruited geriatric nursing assistants from nine aged care institutions in Xi’an and Weinan, Shaanxi Province, China, between May and August 2025. Of 396 returned questionnaires, 330 were included after prespecified data screening. Participants completed measures of perceived organizational climate, four work-motivation dimensions, and work engagement. Pearson correlations, observed-score regressions, four separate structural equation models, and 5,000-resample bias-corrected bootstrap analyses were conducted. Institution- and covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses were also performed. In the joint regression model, intrinsic motivation ( β = 0.420, p < 0.001) and introjected regulation ( β = 0.324, p < 0.001) were independently associated with work engagement, whereas perceived organizational climate, identified regulation, and external regulation were not. Across the four structural equation models, perceived organizational climate was positively associated with each motivation dimension (standardized β = 0.652–0.704), and each motivation dimension was positively associated with work engagement ( β = 0.543–0.771). Because each model included only one motivation dimension, the indirect estimates were model-specific rather than unique contributions independent of the other dimensions. Significant indirect associations were observed through intrinsic motivation ( β = 0.519, bias-corrected 95% CI [0.430, 0.636]), identified regulation ( β = 0.430, [0.349, 0.532]), introjected regulation ( β = 0.530, [0.439, 0.648]), and external regulation ( β = 0.359, [0.258, 0.497]). In separate sensitivity analyses based on standardized observed scores, the four indirect associations remained statistically significant after adjustment for institutions and selected individual-level covariates. Perceived organizational climate and the four work-motivation dimensions were associated with work engagement among geriatric nursing assistants. The findings support further investigation of how organizational conditions and qualitatively different forms of work motivation relate to engagement. Because all variables were measured concurrently, temporal ordering and causal mediation cannot be established.

items.abstract: The study analyzes the potential of generative AI technologies to address students' individual learning needs, differentiate instructional materials, develop English language skills (lexical, grammatical, communicative, and receptive-productive), provide immediate feedback, and support independent learning. The methodological framework of the study comprises systemic, comparative, linguo-didactic, and modeling methods. The results indicate that generative AI tools create additional opportunities for transitioning from a "one-size-fits-all" assignment approach to an individualized and differentiated teaching model in inclusive English language education. At the same time, issues such as the accuracy of AI-generated content, academic integrity, data privacy, the risk of excessive student reliance on AI, and the maintenance of teacher oversight were identified as critical methodological considerations.

items.title: INNOVATIVE APPROACHES TO DEVELOPING STUDENTS' FOREIGN LANGUAGE COMMUNICATIVE COMPETENCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of foreign language communicative competence has become an essential component of contemporary higher education. The increasing internationalization of academic and professional environments requires university students to use foreign languages not only for understanding linguistic information but also for participating effectively in academic discussions, professional communication, intercultural interaction, collaborative projects, and digital communication. This article examines innovative approaches to developing students’ foreign language communicative competence in higher education. Particular attention is given to communicative, task-based, project-based, learner-centered, collaborative, and technology-enhanced approaches. The study analyzes the relationship between linguistic knowledge and practical communicative performance and identifies pedagogical conditions that contribute to students’ active participation in foreign language learning. The role of authentic materials, professional contexts, digital platforms, artificial intelligence, peer interaction, reflective learning, and formative assessment is also considered. The article proposes an integrated pedagogical framework in which foreign language instruction is organized around meaningful communicative tasks, learner autonomy, professional relevance, and continuous feedback. The proposed approach is intended to facilitate students’ transition from controlled language practice to independent and context-sensitive communication. Keywords: foreign language education, communicative competence, university students, innovative approaches, task-based learning, project-based learning, digital technologies, learner autonomy, intercultural communication, formative assessment.

items.title: Integrated approaches to food and beverage safety: assessing contaminants, nutritional quality and emerging detection technologies for public health enhancement
items.abstract: This review synthesises integrated strategies for safeguarding food and beverage safety, with emphasis on emerging contaminants, nutritional quality, and public health implications. Key contaminants, particularly microplastics (MPs) and synthetic dyes, are increasingly detected in packaged foods, bottled water, salt, and beverages, raising significant safety concerns. Recent studies reported a wide variability in MPs contamination across regions and food types, reflecting the absence of standardised detection protocols. Advances in analytical technologies, including nanomaterial-based electrochemical sensors, green microextraction techniques, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted detection platforms, have improved sensitivity and selectivity, although further validation and industrial scalability remain necessary. Similarly, research on synthetic dyes highlights progress in sustainable extraction and detection methods, such as deep eutectic solvent (DES) microextraction and sensor innovation, aligning with the growing shift toward eco-efficient analytical practices. This review also evaluates the nutritional and metabolic impacts of ultra-processed foods (UPFs), which represent a major component of modern diets and are consistently associated with obesity, metabolic syndrome, and other non-communicable diseases. Cross-country analyses revealed excessive sugar, salt, and fat content in UPFs, alongside gaps in front-of-package labelling systems and limited consumer literacy. These findings underscore the need for harmonised nutritional profiling frameworks and product reformulation policies. In addition, the role of probiotics in enhancing microbial safety and functional beverage quality is examined. Emerging microencapsulation techniques show promise in improving probiotic survival and bioactivity during storage and digestion, though mechanistic insights remain limited. Policy assessments indicate that fiscal measures, advertising regulations, and labelling requirements are inconsistently applied across nations, revealing persistent misalignment between technological innovations, regulatory implementation, and consumer behaviour. Three major research gaps are identified: (i) the lack of standardised, validated analytical methods for emerging contaminants; (ii) limited mechanistic understanding of probiotic stability and functionality in beverage systems; and (iii) insufficient integration of culturally adaptive, consumer-centred policy strategies. Future research should prioritise harmonised analytical frameworks, scalable and sustainable detection technologies, a clearer understanding of probiotic mechanisms, and comprehensive nutritional databases. Strong multisectoral collaboration among scientists, industry, and policymakers is crucial to translate these advances into effective public health actions. Collectively, this review highlights the need for an integrated, multidisciplinary approach that unites technological innovation, nutritional science, and evidence-based regulation to ensure the safety of food and beverages worldwide.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and First-Principles Physics for the Discovery of Sustainable Topological Heusler Materials: Prospects for Spintronics and Energy-Efficient Technologies in Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), first-principles computational methods, and advanced functional materials provides new opportunities for the accelerated discovery of energy-efficient quantum and spintronic materials. Heusler alloys are particularly attractive because their chemical composition and structural ordering can be systematically modified to obtain desirable magnetic, electronic, topological, and thermoelectric properties. Magnetic Heusler compounds with strong spin–orbit coupling can exhibit Weyl points, band crossings, Berry-curvature hotspots, and enhanced anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC). Representative literature systems demonstrate the potential of this materials family: Co2MnGa has a reported calculated AHC of approximately −1310 Scm⁻¹, while Co2MnAl reaches approximately −1631 Scm⁻¹; Co2CrAl illustrates strong Fermi-level dependence, with its AHC increasing from approximately −313 Scm⁻¹ to about 1089 Scm⁻¹ after energy tuning. This work proposes an integrated density functional theory (DFT) and AI framework for the systematic discovery and optimization of sustainable topological Heusler materials. DFT calculations provide the physics-based evaluation of structural stability, magnetic ordering, electronic structure, spin–orbit coupling, Berry curvature, AHC, and ANC, while machine-learning models can learn composition–structure–property relationships and accelerate screening across unexplored chemical spaces. The proposed workflow includes stability screening, magnetic-ground-state analysis, electronic and topological characterization, Berry-curvature calculations, anomalous transverse transport calculations, machine-learning prediction, and independent DFT validation. Chemical substitution and carrier tuning are considered as strategies for positioning topological features near the Fermi level and enhancing transverse transport. Literature examples such as Pt2CrRh, with reported AHC of approximately 1966 Scm⁻¹ and ANC of approximately 7.50 Am⁻¹K⁻¹, and (Co0. 8Ni0.2)2FeSn, with reported AHC of approximately −2568 Scm⁻¹ and ANC of approximately 8.27 Am⁻¹K⁻¹, illustrate the potential of chemical tuning for achieving large transverse responses. The proposed DFT–AI strategy can therefore provide an efficient route toward identifying promising materials for spintronics, spin-caloritronics, low-power electronics, and thermal-energy conversion.

items.abstract: The article critically analyzes and scientifically substantiates the paradigm of integrating modern information and communication technologies (ICT) and artificial intelligence (AI) tools into the system of heuristic foreign language teaching in higher education. The author demonstrates that the synergy of digital tools and generative AI serves as a powerful intensifier of the educational process, ensuring deep individualization, differentiation of learning, enhancement of students’ intrinsic motivation, and the development of their cognitive and creative autonomy. The study synthesizes practical experience in utilizing the digital ecosystem of Sumy State Pedagogical University named after A.S. Makarenko in combination with video conferencing services (Google Meet, Zoom) and adaptive AI technologies to organize flexible online learning. Particular attention is paid to the effectiveness of these tools under crisis conditions (the COVID-19 pandemic and martial law) both for the routine automation of assessment and for modeling open-ended creative tasks of an exploratory nature. The paper presents original methodological developments, including the electronic manual «Communicative Culture of Medical Students in Use», integrated with modern digital resources. Specific examples demonstrate how the use of ICT and AI assistants enables students to complete a full heuristic cycle: from analytical information processing to the generation, self-correction, and defense of their own original educational product. The author summarizes the undeniable advantages of the updated innovative higher education space, which transforms traditional subject-subject relations into a format of interactive partnership: “teacher – student – artificial intelligence”.

items.title: Integrating Large Language Models in Foreign Language Teaching: Prompting Advanced English Grammar
items.abstract: Abstract This chapter discusses how Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT can be used in modern foreign language teaching. It focusses on teacher training in integrative approaches that do not see LLMs as supplementary learning, but as part of the central teacher–learner interaction, including autonomous learning in flipped classroom approaches. It is not an empirical study with students, but an empirical play with prompts, the decisive starting point of successful human–machine/artificial intelligence/chatbot interaction. It emphasizes the potential of LLMs for teaching and learning without neglecting ethical concerns and practical challenges. It provides examples from ChatGPT 3–5 and Bard Experiment, now Gemini, to illustrate how LLMs can be used to generate explanations, construct exercises with model answers and even correct exam tests for complex grammatical English constructions such as article usage and modal auxiliaries. This study illustrates where LLMs can be integrated into teacher training to help students in autonomous or teacher-mediated learning, but it also shows clearly that users always have to be well-informed and remain skeptical about LLM suggestions and that even LLMs in their current free versions only provide suggestions that may only be used in revised or adapted form.

items.title: Integrating operational emission management into SMS: A bibliometric and conceptual perspective on the ISM Code
items.abstract: The maritime industry is undergoing a paradigm shift driven by stringent decarbonization regulations, such as the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) and Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI). Despite the proliferation of technical solutions, a conceptual divide persists between emission compliance and the established safety management culture governed by the International Safety Management (ISM) Code. This study employs a comprehensive bibliometric analysis to examine the intellectual structure and evolution of the maritime decarbonization literature. Using a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided selection process, 88 core publications from the Web of Science database were analyzed using R Bibliometrix. Results from the Gompertz growth model suggest a trend toward technical saturation in the literature, pointing to a potential shift toward operational management. Furthermore, factorial and Sankey analyses reveal a significant disconnect between emissions management and Safety Management Systems (SMS), with “human factors” and “safety culture” remaining marginalized as “niche” themes. The findings suggest that decarbonization is currently treated as an external “administrative reporting burden” rather than an organic operational routine. To bridge this gap, this study conceptualizes the pathways for integrating operational emission management into SMS from an ISM Code perspective. Rather than proposing isolated technical data fixes or validated operational software, the study illustrates how fuel inefficiencies can be conceptually evaluated within the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle. This research provides a baseline for policymakers and ship management companies seeking to align environmental performance monitoring with shipboard safety routines.

items.abstract: Background The high variability of workloads makes it very difficult for cloud datacenters to efficiently schedule their tasks and resource allocation. The correct forecasting of future resource utilization allows us to proactively scale and implement more sophisticated scheduling policies, which eventually results in has potential to improve resource utilization and fewer failures. Methods Leveraging only data that is exposed to the scheduler at task dispatch times, this research assesses four supervised learning approaches for estimation of CPU consumption on the Google Cluster Data v3 trace: Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, and a Neural Network. Result The randomized forest version gave the optimum regression performances on a held-out test set (MAE ≈ 0.00233, RMSE ≈ 0.00589, R 2 ≈ 0.895), while an ordinary hybrid composition of the two best systems performed similarly. Estimating if a task’s real CPU consumption surpasses a train-set-derived high utilization threshold which was achieved up to 0.921 accuracy and ≈ 0.844 best F1, chosen via a detailed threshold sweeping as opposed to an individual set cutoff. Conclusions This approach are evaluated using RMSE, MAE, and R 2 for held-out on test set, while the 2nd threshold-based analysis is utilized to appraise the recognition of high-CPU tasks. These results underscore the potential of data driven approach definitely machine and deep learning-based CPU demand predictions as valuable tools for cloud schedulers, improving resource management, and reducing operational costs. items.title: Intention to Adopt Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: Insights from Health Science Students through the Technology Acceptance Model
items.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate health science students’ intentions to adopt artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare and to identify key predictors of these intentions using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 967 students enrolled in various health-related disciplines at a university. Data were collected through a self-administered online questionnaire comprising five sections: demographic information, information technology (IT) skills, perceptions of AI in medicine, attitudes towards AI and intentions to adopt AI in healthcare. Approximately half of the participants reported high intentions to integrate AI into their future medical practice. Linear regression analyses confirmed the applicability of the TAM in predicting AI adoption intentions and identified the following three significant predictors: attitudes towards AI, perceptions of AI in medicine and IT skills. Among these, attitudes towards AI emerged as the strongest predictor (β = 0.563, t = 17.687, p < 0.001). These findings underscore the importance of fostering students’ IT competencies and positive perceptions and attitudes to facilitate the effective integration of AI into medical education and practice. Future research should employ longitudinal designs to examine changes in students’ perceptions and attitudes over time, thereby providing insights for curriculum development that better aligns with students’ evolving learning needs and ensures professional readiness.

items.title: Introducing the LISA Framework: Level and Integration Scope of Artificial Intelligence in Learning Design (Presentation at ICL 2026, Cologne, 09/2026)
items.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming learning design, yet current terminology often lacks the precision to distinguish between varying levels of AI involvement. Terms like "AI-supported" obscure critical differences in decision-making authority and adaptation dynamism. This presentation introduces the LISA Framework (Level of autonomy and Interaction Scope of AI in learning design), developed within the Erasmus+ project DigiSET. LISA proposes a two-dimensional typology based on (1) the Level of AI Autonomy (human-led assistance to fully autonomous operation) and (2) the Interaction Scope (static, rule-based execution vs. dynamic, comprehensive adaptation). Six archetypes emerge: the Content Generator, the Co-Creator, the Rule-Based Agent, the Smart Assistant, the Adaptive Partner, and the Autonomous Agent. Grounded in practical experiences from Graz University of Technology, this heuristic model provides educators, researchers, and policymakers with a structured vocabulary to analyze, discuss, and strategically plan AI-enhanced learning resources. This paper was presented by Benedikt Brünner. Citation: Schön, S., Brünner, B.& Ebner, M. (2026, September 30). items.title: Knowing more, doing less: AI literacy development and organisational barriers in healthcare training
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how healthcare professionals responsible for training (HPRTs) interpret and appropriate artificial intelligence (AI)-focused pedagogical resources within their workplace context, addressing the knowing-doing gap: the pattern whereby increased awareness of AI tools does not straightforwardly translate into changed practice and may recalibrate professional confidence even as perceived relevance increases. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative intervention design was used at the Centre hospitalier de l’Université de Montréal (CHUM). Six participants of differing prior AI experience engaged with an eight-week intervention delivering pedagogical guides and microlearning videos. Data were collected through two focus group discussions conducted in French and analysed on original transcripts using reflexive thematic analysis, with Illeris’s workplace learning theory as primary sensitising framework, alongside situated expectancy-value, personal construct and agency theories, drawn on iteratively. Findings Three findings emerged, differentiated by participant experience level: (1) expectancy recalibration, in which increased knowledge accompanied decreased confidence, marking accommodative learning; (2) principled boundary-setting, through which professionals differentiated between appropriate and inappropriate AI uses; and (3) organisational conditions, namely, tool access, protected time and institutional endorsement, as important structural mediators of literacy development. Originality/value The study conceptualises the knowing-doing gap as an emergent structural feature of AI literacy development under real organisational conditions, extending the literature by documenting learners’ experience of that gap. Reduced confidence may signal more differentiated professional judgment rather than failure. Individual learning capacity requires an infrastructure of agency for realisation. These findings challenge adoption-centric models of professional AI literacy.

items.title: Knowing with the Machine: Towards an Epistemology of Research Augmented by Large Language Models in the Social Sciences
items.abstract: The entry of large language models (LLMs) into social science research practices, such as interview coding, literature reviews, hypothesis generation and the simulation of respondents, is usually discussed from a technical or ethical standpoint. This paper offers an epistemological reading. It argues that an LLM is neither a neutral instrument nor a "co-researcher", but an interpretive mediator whose probabilistic and opaque outputs affect the criteria of rigour differently depending on the paradigm adopted. By confronting LLM uses with the positivist, critical realist, interpretivist and constructivist paradigms, the paper shows that each paradigm calls for specific safeguards. It then proposes a protocol for comparing human and algorithmic coding, followed by a five-dimension rigour framework (traceability, reproducibility, reflexivity, adversarial validation and interpretive accountability) specified for each paradigm. The contribution is twofold. Theoretically, the paper brings generative AI into the debate on the foundations of knowledge in the social sciences. Methodologically, it provides researchers and reviewers with a tool to assess the legitimacy of AI-assisted research.

items.title: La inteligencia artificial sobre el rendimiento académico en estudiantes de tercero bachillerato
items.abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial en el bachillerato transforma la búsqueda de información, la realización de tareas y la comprensión de contenidos, aunque también plantea riesgos de dependencia, uso acrítico y afectación de la integridad académica. El estudio tiene como objetivo analizar la influencia percibida de la inteligencia artificial sobre el rendimiento académico de los estudiantes de tercero de bachillerato de la Unidad Educativa Cristiana Nazareno. Se emplea un enfoque mixto secuencial, iniciado con una revisión documental cualitativa y continuado con una fase cuantitativa mediante una encuesta estructurada con escala Likert; el diseño es no experimental, transversal y de alcance exploratorio-descriptivo, con una muestra censal de 32 estudiantes. La simulación de resultados muestra que 21 participantes utilizan inteligencia artificial frecuentemente o siempre, 17 prefieren ChatGPT, 22 la emplean para investigar y 21 perciben mejoras en la comprensión y el aprendizaje; asimismo, 22 reconocen riesgo de dependencia. Estos hallazgos evidencian una valoración favorable, aunque no permiten establecer causalidad entre uso de inteligencia artificial y calificaciones. Se concluye que estas herramientas constituyen un apoyo académico relevante, siempre que se integren con orientación docente, verificación de información y criterios de uso responsable.

items.title: Language of Toxicity: An eXplainable Artificial Intelligence Approach
items.abstract: Abstract Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure–activity relationships. Here, we present a descriptor-free, language-inspired framework that can be applied to different toxicity prediction tasks within a unified architecture. The model proposed combines a multiscale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer to capture chemical patterns at different scales and a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layer to capture the sequential nature of these patterns. This architecture also exploits an attention mechanism that computes attention weights across the sequence, enabling the model to focus on the most relevant molecular substructures for toxicity prediction. Toxic and nontoxic chemicals, represented by canonical SMILES, are investigated as the words of two languages which have to be discriminated; using eight different end points, the model provided an accurate description of toxicity patterns, with an average Area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.83 (min: 0.70, max: 0.94) under repeated cross-validation. The models were trained on relatively small data sets (∼1000 samples) and often strongly imbalanced, two important challenges that highlight the opportunities for future improvement; moreover, the proposed attention-based framework offers a representation of the molecular regions influencing model predictions, providing a basis for future investigations into toxicity-related structural patterns and potentially supporting hypothesis generation in drug design or drug repurposing applications.

items.title: Large-language-model-based white spot analysis of patent landscapes in emerging battery technologies
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of scientific publications and patent filings challenges conventional approaches for systematically assessing technological progress in emerging energy storage technologies. Here, we present an artificial intelligence-assisted patent analytics framework to identify technology-specific research gaps (“white spots”), using zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) and organic electrode materials (OEMs) as representative case studies. Patents were classified across multiple analytical dimensions, including materials, battery chemistries, and key performance indicators (KPIs). Three analytically distinct types of white spots are identified: limited absolute patenting activity within a given category (activity white spots), insufficient quantitative performance disclosure despite active patenting (reporting white spots), and disproportionate reliance on knowledge transferred from adjacent battery fields (knowledge-flow white spots). The analysis reveals a strong dominance of aqueous electrolyte concepts in ZIBs, accounting for 1883 patents, while non-aqueous and solid electrolytes remain underrepresented. Citation network analysis further shows that innovation in these underexplored electrolyte classes relies disproportionately on knowledge originating from adjacent battery technologies. For OEMs, up to 93% of the 368 patents focus on lithium-based chemistries, which exhibit the most comprehensive quantitative reporting. In contrast, sodium-based and all-solid-state systems are characterized by substantial gaps in KPI disclosure, limiting cross-chemistry benchmarking. Overall, the results demonstrate that white spots in emerging battery technologies arise not only at the materials level, but also from asymmetric knowledge flows and incomplete performance reporting. The here proposed framework provides a scalable tool for mapping technological maturity and supporting research strategies in next-generation energy storage systems.

items.title: Latent profile analysis of artificial intelligence anxiety among undergraduate nursing students: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Aim/objective This study aimed to classify subgroups of artificial intelligence (AI) anxiety among nursing undergraduates using latent profile analysis, describe their demographic characteristics, and identify factors associated membership in each latent profile. Background Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely implemented in clinical nursing practice, but nursing undergraduates often experience AI anxiety, which impedes their adaptation to smart medical services. Few existing studies have stratified students according to anxiety levels to formulate targeted intervention measures. Design A cross-sectional study. Methods Participants were 526 nursing undergraduates recruited from several medical colleges in Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, and Sichuan provinces as well as Chongqing Municipality, China. Questionnaires, including a general information questionnaire, the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale, and the Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy Questionnaire, were distributed. Mplus version 8.3 was used for latent profile analysis, and multinomial logistic regression was performed to analyze factors associated with profile membership. Results A total of 526 students were included. The total AI anxiety score was 57.76 ± 15.94, indicating a moderate level of AI anxiety. AI anxiety among undergraduate nursing students was classified into three latent profiles: the low AI anxiety group (53.2%), moderate AI anxiety group (12.7%), and high AI anxiety group (34.0%). Multinomial logistic regression analysis showed that gender, participation in AI-related education or courses, attitude toward AI, and monthly household income (Renminbi [RMB]) were independently associated with membership in latent profiles among undergraduate nursing students with AI anxiety ( p < 0.05). Conclusion Nursing undergraduates present distinct heterogeneous patterns of AI anxiety. These findings may help identify students with elevated AI anxiety and inform individualized educational interventions.

items.title: LAWSONE: AN INTEGRATED REVIEW OF CHEMICAL RESEARCH, ANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES, AI APPLICATIONS, AND SAFETY
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Lawsone is a naturally occurring naphthoquinone mainly obtained from the leaves of Lawsonia inermis (henna). It is responsible for the characteristic orange-red colour of henna and has attracted interest because of its chemical reactivity, natural origin, analytical importance and biological properties. Chemically, lawsone is known as 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone and contains a conjugated quinone system with hydroxyl and carbonyl functional groups. This review summarizes the botanical sources, chemical composition, synthesis, physicochemical properties and major analytical techniques used for lawsone. TLC, HPTLC, HPLC, UV-Visible spectroscopy, FT-IR, LC-MS/MS, GC-MS and NMR techniques are discussed for identification and quality assessment. The application of artificial intelligence and machine learning in chemical and analytical research is also highlighted. Safety aspects of lawsone and henna preparations are briefly discussed. Overall, lawsone remains an important natural quinone with applications in pharmaceutical, cosmetic, analytical and organic chemical research.

items.title: Learner Agency and the Negotiation of EFL Motivation in GenAI ‐Mediated Drama‐Based Learning: A Qualitative Case Study
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping language learning environments, yet little is known about how it becomes embedded within learners' motivational and agentive experiences in collaborative, informal settings like English drama‐based learning. This qualitative case study examines EFL learners' motivation during a 12‐week GenAI‐mediated English drama production cycle in a Chinese university drama club. Guided by Dörnyei's (2009) L2 Motivational Self System (L2MSS), the analysis examines learners' accounts of the Ideal L2 Self, Ought‐to L2 Self, and L2 Learning Experience alongside three analytic patterns of agency identified in this case: authorship, judgment, and collaboration. Data were drawn from focus groups, individual interviews, drama scripts, GenAI interaction artifacts, and rehearsal observations. Findings indicate that participants experienced GenAI as part of their motivational ecology, particularly in relation to access to advanced language, emerging reference points for “good English,” and the ways collaborative decisions were negotiated. Participants also described different ways of maintaining ownership, evaluating GenAI‐generated language, and coordinating decisions with others. The study extends L2 motivational research by revealing how L2MSS dimensions acquire context‐specific meanings in GenAI‐mediated drama‐based language learning and underscores the importance of fostering critical judgment and sustained human collaboration in GenAI‐supported language learning.

items.title: Learning Analytics and Big Data
items.abstract: Student Engagement refers to the degree to which learners actively participate in educational activities, interact with learning resources, communicate with teachers and peers, and remain involved in the learning process. In digital education, Learning Analytics can provide systematic methods for observing and analysing different forms of student engagement. Traditional measures of engagement often depend on classroom observation, attendance, participation, assignments, and teacher feedback. Digital learning environments can provide additional information through learning management systems, online assessments, discussion platforms, virtual laboratories, educational applications, and connected learning devices. Learning Analytics can transform these data into meaningful information that helps teachers understand patterns of participation and identify opportunities to support student learning. A simplified framework is: Student Activity → Data Collection → Learning Analytics → Engagement Pattern → Teacher Interpretation → Educational SupportThe purpose of engagement analytics should not be simply to count student activities. The central goal is to understand whether students are meaningfully participating in learning and whether additional support may be required. Student engagement represents the learner's active involvement in the educational process. It can include: Participation Attention Interaction Motivation Collaboration Persistence Completion of learning activities Engagement is multidimensional and cannot be completely represented by a single numerical indicator. Student engagement is commonly considered through several dimensions: Behavioural engagement Cognitive engagement Emotional engagement Social engagement These dimensions can interact with one another. Behavioural engagement refers to observable participation in learning activities. Examples include: Attending classes Completing assignments Participating in activities Submitting assessments Accessing learning resources Digital systems can record some of these activities. Cognitive engagement refers to the mental effort students invest in understanding and applying knowledge.

items.title: Learning Analytics and Big Data
items.abstract: Student Engagement refers to the degree to which learners actively participate in educational activities, interact with learning resources, communicate with teachers and peers, and remain involved in the learning process. In digital education, Learning Analytics can provide systematic methods for observing and analysing different forms of student engagement. Traditional measures of engagement often depend on classroom observation, attendance, participation, assignments, and teacher feedback. Digital learning environments can provide additional information through learning management systems, online assessments, discussion platforms, virtual laboratories, educational applications, and connected learning devices. Learning Analytics can transform these data into meaningful information that helps teachers understand patterns of participation and identify opportunities to support student learning. A simplified framework is: Student Activity → Data Collection → Learning Analytics → Engagement Pattern → Teacher Interpretation → Educational SupportThe purpose of engagement analytics should not be simply to count student activities. The central goal is to understand whether students are meaningfully participating in learning and whether additional support may be required. Student engagement represents the learner's active involvement in the educational process. It can include: Participation Attention Interaction Motivation Collaboration Persistence Completion of learning activities Engagement is multidimensional and cannot be completely represented by a single numerical indicator. Student engagement is commonly considered through several dimensions: Behavioural engagement Cognitive engagement Emotional engagement Social engagement These dimensions can interact with one another. Behavioural engagement refers to observable participation in learning activities. Examples include: Attending classes Completing assignments Participating in activities Submitting assessments Accessing learning resources Digital systems can record some of these activities. Cognitive engagement refers to the mental effort students invest in understanding and applying knowledge.

items.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development of Azo Dye-Based Metal Complexes with Antimicrobial Properties
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities for accelerating scientific research, particularly in materials science, medicinal chemistry, coordination chemistry, and sustainable chemical development. Azo dye-based metal complexes represent an important class of coordination compounds because of their diverse structural characteristics, tunable electronic properties, and potential biological activities. However, conventional synthesis and screening of such complexes can be time-consuming, resource-intensive, and dependent on extensive experimental trials. The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning can provide an efficient approach for predicting molecular properties, optimizing synthesis conditions, and identifying compounds with enhanced antimicrobial potential. The present study proposes an AI-assisted framework for the sustainable development of azo dye-based metal complexes with antimicrobial properties. In this approach, molecular descriptors, structural characteristics, physicochemical properties, metal-ion characteristics, and experimentally determined antimicrobial data can be integrated into machine-learning models. These models can be trained to establish structure–activity relationships and predict the antimicrobial performance of newly designed complexes before their experimental synthesis. Such predictive modelling may help researchers prioritize promising compounds and reduce unnecessary laboratory experimentation. The proposed approach also supports the principles of green and sustainable chemistry by potentially reducing chemical consumption, solvent use, energy requirements, experimental repetitions, and laboratory waste. AI can further assist in optimizing reaction parameters such as temperature, reaction time, solvent, pH, reactant ratio, and catalyst concentration to improve yield and efficiency. The integration of AI with coordination chemistry can therefore contribute to the development of safer, more efficient, and environmentally responsible antimicrobial materials. The approach is particularly relevant to India's emerging digital scientific ecosystem, where AI-enabled research can support innovation, reduce research costs, and strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration between chemistry, computational science, biotechnology, and data science. The study concludes that AI should be viewed as a complementary tool to experimental chemistry rather than a replacement for laboratory validation. Combining computational prediction with synthesis, characterization, and antimicrobial evaluation can provide a powerful pathway for developing novel azo dye-based metal complexes while supporting sustainable scientific development.

items.title: Leveraging on Artificial Intelligence Technology in Boosting Cassava Production in Nigeria: The Gains and Constraints
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology is reshaping agricultural landscape globally by employing data-driven, efficient, and scalable production methods. Nigeria, as the world’s largest producer of cassava, faces persistent challenges like low yield per hectare, pest infestations, climate variability, and inefficient farming techniques. This study focuses on the potential of AI technology to exploit and enhance the nation’s agricultural potentials and productivity. The study decisively examines the application of AI in cassava production in Nigeria, focusing on its gains and constraints. It adopted ways to addressing the critical challenges like climate variability, scarce access to digital farming techniques, and the need for sustainable practices. Using a descriptive and analytical approach based on secondary data from FAO, NBS, IITA, and recent scholarly publications, the study explores AI-driven technologies such as precision agriculture, machine learning, remote sensing, and automation. Findings from the study reveal that AI technology application in cassava production can significantly improve productivity, optimize resource utilization, and reduce post-harvest losses. However, adoption can be constrained by high costs, poor infrastructure, low digital literacy, and weak policy frameworks. This paper investigates how AI technology can be employed to achieve the mass production of cassava in Nigeria, while critically examining the associated gains or benefits and constraints.

items.title: Lightweight Edge-AI Model for Real-Time Sorghum Disease Detection on Resource-Constrained Mobile Devices
items.abstract: Lightweight Edge-AI Model for Real-Time Sorghum Disease Detection on Resource-Constrained Mobile Devices presents an efficient artificial intelligence approach for identifying sorghum diseases directly on mobile and edge-computing platforms. The study focuses on developing a lightweight machine learning model capable of performing rapid and accurate disease detection while operating under limited computational resources, memory, and power constraints. Computer vision and deep learning techniques are used to analyse sorghum leaf images and distinguish healthy plants from diseased conditions. Model optimization strategies are considered to reduce computational complexity and improve inference speed without substantially compromising detection performance. The proposed approach supports real-time, on-device disease diagnosis, reducing dependence on cloud connectivity and enabling timely intervention in agricultural environments. The work highlights the potential of Edge AI and mobile computing to make intelligent crop monitoring more accessible, practical, and scalable, particularly for farmers and agricultural users operating in resource-constrained settings.

items.title: LLM-Supported Hybrid Reranking Architecture for Candidate-Job Matching in Recruitment Processes
items.abstract: Traditional applicant tracking systems miss candidates' potential due to their keyword-based structures, while pure large language model approaches carry high costs and hallucination risks. This study proposes a hybrid architecture that integrates vector-based semantic search with data validation steps and delivers the final decision through a large language model-based reranking module to overcome these issues. The proposed system processes candidate data through a multi-stage filtering funnel by separating structured and unstructured formats. Experimental analysis on a real-world dataset comprising 52 job postings and 36 candidate resumes demonstrates that this hybrid approach achieves a retrieval success rate of 91.67%, a human resources expert scoring alignment of 86.11%, and a mean absolute error of 0.200, significantly outperforming traditional applicant tracking systems and pure large language model methods in both accuracy and cost-efficiency. The findings show that the architecture achieves high retrieval success and scoring alignment, offering an explainable, scalable, and accurate decision support system for human resources processes. Ultimately, this study bridges the gap between theoretical RAG capabilities and practical human resources deployment, presenting a reliable framework for next-generation recruitment.

items.title: Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container
items.abstract: Remembering the path you did not take does not mean you lived it. Forgetting why you chose a path does not restore your exhausted body. Let us begin the consciousness puzzle with this asymmetry. Why does red feel red? Before asking that, let us ask another question: when did that red become an event, and whose event did it become? This paper calls the causal structure that sustains a single present and history the “subjective container.” It searches for its location while keeping this task separate from explaining how qualia arise. Our tool is subtraction. Place a body, an environment, and viability constraints on the board, then remove the relations one by one. Selection may remain, but without something that bears its consequences, whose event it is remains unspecified. Change may remain, but without continuation from that change, no connected history follows. This “proof by absence” narrows down the necessary roles. What remains is a framework in which competing candidates close into one outcome, and the same system bears its consequences and continues. The losers lose their standing to determine the continuation at this juncture; the winner’s causal efficacy carries forward into the conditions for what comes next. This is called “temporal closure.” The “convergence point” that sustains this linkage is strongly inferred to be the location of the subjective container. History operates not only as a stored record but also as present conditions that reshape subsequent possibilities. Moreover, this “internal reference point” may participate not only after a winner has been selected, but also in candidate competition and the formation of content. Does the container merely receive a ready-made red? Or is it part of the process through which red takes shape? If another structure is added to make the event belong to a subject, what does it newly explain? This “double retention problem” uses Occam’s principle to examine the explanation, then extends the puzzle to the role of brains, existing theories, and the design of artificial consciousness. This is a perspective paper developed through dialogue with generative AI by a disability welfare worker with no academic background in consciousness research. It offers neither experimental validation nor a deductive proof of identity with consciousness. Why red feels red remains unresolved. But perhaps we can narrow down where to ask that question.
